- Do you require a public static IP for the service endpoints or will the deployment live entirely behind our NAT?

- Which ports need to be open inbound from your side (if any) vs outbound from our side?
- Do you need us to create service accounts ahead of time? If so, what fields/format?
- KMS/Key rotation: we will likely need an external KMS key or cross-account access; what's supported?

We also need to understand egress bandwidth and whether there are any keepalive/MTU requirements for heavy model requests.

Can we schedule a 30–45 minute technical handoff next week with your network/infra engineer? We can invite our networking and security leads.

Alice — great, thanks for the inventory. I'll get a technical handoff scheduled.

Quick answers up-front so your team can start validating:
- Redwood can operate behind your NAT (egress-only) or via VPC peering/VPN. For lowest latency we recommend VPC peering where available; VPN is fine if peering is not possible.
- Typical required outbound ports from the customer VPC: 443 (to Redwood control endpoints), 443/80 for model downloads only during provisioning, and UDP/123 for NTP if you restrict outbound NTP. We do NOT need inbound ports opened except for SSH to a customer-hosted bastion if you opt to host jump boxes.
- Service account CSV template attached (service-account-template.csv). Please populate principal email and desired role scope.
- For KMS we support cross-account KMS policies and customer-managed keys; Rishi will follow up with exact principal ARNs we need.

I'll propose times for the technical call. If your networking folks prefer, we can also provide a short preflight checklist for the meeting so we can run through items quickly.

Best,

Hi Alice / Permacare networking team — I'm Rishi (Inference Infra). A few technical clarifications and our recommended defaults so you can validate with your ops team before the call:

1) Connectivity model:
- Preferred: VPC peering (private, no NAT traversal); we'll ask you to add our peering CIDR (we'll share it once the account is provisioned).
- Fallback: IPsec VPN with BGP — acceptable but expect slightly higher latency and keepalive tuning.

2) IPs / ports:
- Outbound only required: 443 to endpoints in your region.
- Optional: 22 to your bastion host for operators if you need us to SSH in for troubleshooting (we strongly prefer using your bastion/jump host and we do not request direct inbound to managed hosts).
- Metrics/observability: outbound TCP 9000 (Prometheus push) OR HTTP(S) push to an ingest endpoint — we can adapt to either.

3) MTU / fragmentation:
- We recommend 1500 MTU end-to-end; if you're using an overlay (GRE/VXLAN) set MTU accordingly (1460–1480 typical).

4) DNS & certs:
- You'll need an internal DNS entry (A/CNAME) for any managed endpoints we expose; TLS termination is handled by Redwood with customer-provided certs if required.

5) KMS & keys:
- If you're bringing your own KMS key, we'll need the key ARN and a policy to allow the Redwood principal to encrypt/decrypt. If not, we can manage keys and provide attestations.

6) Service accounts:
- Please use the attached service-account-template.csv. Minimum fields: principal_email, role, owner, expiration (optional). Roles we need: network-reader, kms-encryptor, secrets-uploader.

I've attached an initial network diagram (network-diagram-v1.png) that shows the recommended peering topology and NAT boundaries.

Happy to talk through any of the above on the call. Proposed slots: Tue 11/24 10:00–10:45 PT or Wed 11/25 14:00–14:45 PT. What works?

- Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all — Dev here from the Private Deploy team. Quick preflight checklist that we'll run during the technical handoff and that you can validate beforehand: 

1) Account & IAM
- Please populate service-account-template.csv with the principal_email and role columns. We'll need one service account for admin operations and one for metrics ingestion.
- Minimum role set we request: network-reader, kms-access (Encrypt/Decrypt limited), secret-uploader.

2) Networking
- Confirm chosen connectivity: VPC peering preferred. If peering unavailable, provide VPN endpoints and BGP ASNs.
- Provide egress firewall rule allowing outbound 443 to our endpoints and outbound 9000/HTTP for metrics.
- Provide MTU for the peered path and any overlay tunnel configs.

3) Security
- If using customer KMS, share key ARN and add grant to redwood-infra@redwood-infra-prod (we'll provide exact principal on the call).
- TLS: we'll accept customer-provided cert (PEM) or we can provision a cert for internal endpoints; confirm what you prefer.

4) Ops & monitoring
- Add the following hosts to your allowlist for health checks: health-us-1.redwood-inference.com (we'll provide final IP ranges).
- SNMP/Netflow not required; syslog forwarding can be set up later if you want audit logs exported.

Links: runbook draft — https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c_redwood_private_onboard

We'll review this on Tue 11/24 10:00 PT. Thanks for attaching your CIDR list and inventory; that will speed the discussion.
